record.original_question: Fix Lambda >= 0 and a sequence of resonances z(hbar) whose imaginary parts satisfy Im z(hbar) / hbar -> -Lambda / 2. Which Lambda-eigenmeasures can occur as semiclassical measures of the corresponding metastable states, and is there a favored or even unique limiting measure?

evidence.quote: The above theorem shows that any semiclassical measure is necessarily a Lambda-eigenmeasure, with decay rate Lambda equal to the asymptotic quantum decay rates. In view of the quantum ergodicity result for chaotic closed systems, the following question naturally arises: Given Lambda >= 0, and considering a sequence of resonances (z(hbar)) satisfying (67), which Lambda-eigenmeasures can be obtained as semiclassical measures? Is there a "favoured" limit, or even a unique one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold (or more generally a phase space carrying a chaotic Hamiltonian flow $\Phi^t$ on an energy shell $\mathcal{E}\subset T^*M$), and consider a semiclassical Schrödinger-type operator $P(\hbar)$ whose classical dynamics on $\mathcal{E}$ is hyperbolic and open (so trajectories may escape to infinity). For $\hbar\to 0^+$, let $z(\hbar)\in\mathbb{C}$ be a sequence of quantum resonances of $P(\hbar)$ with associated metastable (resonant) states $u_\hbar$, normalized on a fixed bounded region. Fix a constant $\Lambda\ge 0$ and assume the resonances satisfy
$$\frac{\operatorname{Im} z(\hbar)}{\hbar} \longrightarrow -\frac{\Lambda}{2}\qquad\text{as }\hbar\to 0^+.$$
A positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{E}$ is called a $\Lambda$-eigenmeasure if it is supported on the trapped set of $\Phi^t$ and satisfies the conditional invariance relation
$$(\Phi^t)_*\mu = e^{-\Lambda t}\,\mu\qquad\text{for all }t\ge 0.$$
A semiclassical measure of the sequence $(u_\hbar)$ is any weak-$*$ limit of the Wigner distributions $W_\hbar[u_\hbar]$. It is known that every such semiclassical measure is a $\Lambda$-eigenmeasure with the prescribed decay rate $\Lambda$.

Question: Characterize precisely which $\Lambda$-eigenmeasures $\mu$ on the trapped set can be realized as semiclassical measures of some sequence $(u_\hbar)$ of metastable states associated to resonances $z(\hbar)$ with $\operatorname{Im} z(\hbar)/\hbar\to -\Lambda/2$. In particular, does there exist a distinguished ("favored") $\Lambda$-eigenmeasure that always arises in this way, and is the limiting semiclassical measure unique under generic chaotic assumptions?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024) on the semiclassical limit of resonance states in chaotic scattering generalizes Ulam's matrix approximation of the Perron–Frobenius operator to construct conditionally invariant ($\Lambda$-eigen) measures at any prescribed decay rate, and provides a conjectural criterion selecting a favored limiting measure, supported by numerical convergence of resonance states to it. Multifractal structure of these states has also been described. However, uniqueness of the limit and a complete classification of admissible $\Lambda$-eigenmeasures remains conjectural in general; the question is partially understood but not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical Limit of Resonance States in Chaotic Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: We construct the conditionally invariant measure that describes the structure of chaotic resonance states of a given decay rate in the semiclassical limit... we conjecture a criterion for selecting the one relevant for resonance states.
status_evidence.claim: A favored conditionally invariant ($\Lambda$-eigen) measure is conjectured and numerically supported, but uniqueness remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical Limit of Resonance States in Chaotic Scattering (HTML)
status_evidence.snippet: Resonance states in quantum chaotic scattering systems have a multifractal structure that depends on their decay rate; classical dynamics describes resonance states of all decay rates in the semiclassical limit.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural classification of $\Lambda$-eigenmeasures arising as semiclassical limits is available.
